title: Add OpenTelemetry tracing + structured logging with safe redaction defaults
author: Monica Patel
release_notes: - Quickstart templates now emit OTel traces and structured logs by default (safe-by-default redaction).
description:
Motivation: We want quickstart templates to be production-minded by default. Today the scaffold has minimal logging and no distributed tracing, which makes it hard to: (a) debug streaming/network failures, (b) attribute latency to retrieval vs model vs tool execution, and (c) align with Redwood Console/SRE expectations for minimum viable signals. This PR introduces OpenTelemetry tracing and structured JSON logging for the Python RAG/agent template, with redaction turned on by default to avoid leaking secrets/PII.

What’s included (Python template): 1) OpenTelemetry tracing: Adds a small instrumentation module that configures an OTel TracerProvider + OTLP exporter (grpc/http) and wires it into the app lifecycle. We emit a predictable span hierarchy for request handling and core RAG/agent steps. Default exporter is OTLP to a local collector; if RW_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is unset we fall back to console span exporter for a “works out of the box” dev experience. 2) Structured logging: Switches template logging to structured JSON with a consistent field set and correlation IDs. Logs are emitted at INFO by default and include request_id + trace_id/span_id when available. 3) Redaction defaults: Adds a redaction filter that aggressively strips common secret patterns (API keys, Bearer tokens), and disables prompt/document/tool payload logging by default. Developers can opt-in to more verbose logging with explicit env vars (see below). 4) Correlation IDs: Captures and propagates Redwood request IDs (x-redwood-request-id / request_id in SDK responses) into logs and span attributes, enabling support escalation workflows and Console filtering.

Span model (high level): - http.server (framework span, when available) - quickstart.request (manual wrapper span; normalizes attributes) - rag.retrieve (retriever call; records chunk count, top_k) - rag.rerank (if enabled; placeholder span only in this PR) - llm.generate (Redwood API call) - agent.loop (outer loop span) - tool.call (per tool invocation; records tool.name and success/failure)

Span attributes (safe + low-cardinality): - service.name=redwood-quickstart - quickstart.template=rag-agent-python - quickstart.template_version (stamped by scaffold) - redwood.request_id (from response header/metadata when available) - llm.provider=redwood - llm.model (configured model name) - llm.stream=true|false - llm.tokens.prompt / llm.tokens.completion (only if returned by API; no tokenization performed in-template) - rag.top_k / rag.chunk_count - tool.name / tool.success

Explicitly NOT captured: - Prompt text, retrieved document content, tool arguments/results (unless opt-in) - User identifiers/emails (callers can add in their app, but template avoids high-cardinality defaults)

Logging field conventions: - level, ts, msg - request_id (best-effort; Redwood request id if present, otherwise generated UUID per inbound request) - trace_id, span_id - template, template_version, env (dev/prod) - error.type, error.message, error.stack (when present) - event (short machine-parsable event name, e.g. rag.retrieve.complete)

Env vars introduced: - RW_OTEL_ENABLED (default: true) - RW_OTEL_EXPORTER (otlp|console; default: otlp if endpoint set, else console) - RW_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (e.g. http://localhost:4318) - RW_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (optional; for auth, format: k=v,k2=v2; redacted in logs) - RW_LOG_LEVEL (default: INFO) - RW_LOG_FORMAT (json|pretty; default: json) - RW_LOG_REDACTION (default: true) - RW_LOG_INCLUDE_PROMPTS (default: false) - RW_LOG_INCLUDE_TOOL_PAYLOADS (default: false)

Implementation notes: - The instrumentation is intentionally lightweight and self-contained under src/observability/ so other templates can copy the module with minimal churn. - We avoid framework auto-instrumentation defaults that can explode cardinality (e.g., capturing full URLs including query params). Where auto-instrumentation is used, we apply minimal config and rely on our own wrapper span for stable naming/attributes. - Redaction is applied at the logger sink and also to any exception context that might include headers (common in HTTP client errors). - All new code paths have unit tests for redaction behavior and for “trace context present -> logs include trace_id”.

Docs: Updates README with: (1) how to run with local console exporter, (2) how to point to a collector, (3) how to verify you’re emitting traces/logs without leaking sensitive data.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Wire in metrics (counters/histograms) aligned with observability-hooks-standard. - Add docker-compose collector + dashboards (tracked in ENG-4184). - Expand TS template parity once pr-108 lands.

Checklist: - [x] Traces emitted with stable span names - [x] Logs are JSON and redact secrets by default - [x] Correlation IDs present in logs and spans - [x] Unit tests for redaction and correlation behavior - [x] README updated with verification steps
commits: observability: add otel bootstrap + exporter selection (console/otlp)
logging: switch to structured JSON logging w/ correlation fields
security: add redaction filter + opt-in verbose payload logging flags
instrumentation: add spans for retrieval, llm.generate, agent/tool loop
docs: update README with local verification + troubleshooting
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Span names/attrs look good overall. Two asks: (1) please avoid putting full model version strings in attributes if they include commit hashes (cardinality). (2) can we standardize request id attribute as redwood.request_id (not request.id)?

Monica Patel (author): Updated attributes: llm.model is now the configured model name only (no build hash); request id attribute renamed to redwood.request_id everywhere. Also added a short note in README about cardinality + what to avoid adding.

Christine Wong (review): Redaction defaults are the right direction. I’m concerned about accidental header logging on http client errors. Can we ensure any exception path that logs headers runs through the redactor?

Monica Patel (author): Good catch. Wrapped the http client exception logging to pass through sanitize_dict() and added a regression test that simulates an httpx exception containing Authorization + x-api-key. Test fails before, passes now.

Caleb Johnson (review): Minor: Please include trace_id/span_id in every log record once context exists (not only in a subset). Also prefer OTLP HTTP endpoint examples in docs since that’s what most users run locally.
Monica Patel (author): Done. Logger now injects trace context via a processor; README updated to show http://localhost:4318 and mentions grpc alternative.
Wei Chen (docs review): README section looks good. Requested one sentence clarifying that prompts/docs are not logged unless explicitly enabled.
Monica Patel (author): Added to README + quickstart troubleshooting section.
Dana Lo (review): Looks compatible with the TS parity work; +1. Might want to keep the observability module interface stable (init_tracing(), init_logging()).
Monica Patel (author): Agreed; kept function names stable and added docstrings noting expected usage.
